findings.evidence: ## When to use restates the description: "When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result."
findings.fix: Delete the When to use section and record the removal; the description already carries the trigger, and the body is invisible until the skill has loaded.

findings.evidence: The per-host routing file repeats one identical foreground command for Claude Code and for every other host, and marks pi, opencode, cursor, codex and copilot unverified with no host-specific step.
findings.fix: Keep the Claude Code completion-notice rule and the one foreground command; collapse the five unverified host headings into the existing 'host without a background primitive' section and record the removed headings.

findings.evidence: Pitfalls lists specific landmines (ignored is not a failure, no idle watchdog, pi +0 bytes, stop only through the lane's own launch) but has no heading a caller can scan as Gotchas, and the executor-guard bullets are adjacent checkout rules rather than runner gotchas.
findings.fix: Rename Pitfalls to Gotchas and keep the runner landmines with their reasons; move the executor-guard and atomic-rewrite bullets to the skill that owns those writes, or record that removal.

findings.evidence: The description names the runner, exit 75 and 69, retry_after_s and the never-switch rule, but not the settings-report reasons a caller must act on (id_carries, mode_forbids, no_slot) or the words settings report.
findings.fix: Use when you run, wait for, read, retry or chain an external AI CLI (pi, opencode, codex, cursor, copilot, claude) through ai-kit's cross-AI runner (cross-ai.mjs): pick one runtime and model, pass the call's settings (role, effort, context, session id, skills, MCP servers), launch the runner, read its exit code, its per-setting report (applied, ignored, unknown, including id_carries, mode_forbids and no_slot) and its last AIKIT-XAI stderr line, resume a session in a second round, and answer a stop. Also use when a lane hits quota, a rate limit or a 429, exits 75 or 69, prints retry_after_s=, reports a setting ignored, or needs an --argv-file for a CLI the runner has no formula for. Covers the hard-tier wait, the user notice, GSD's retry/skip/abort answer and the rule to never switch harness, provider or model. Not for reviewer setup or GSD config (those are ai-kit-spec-config and ai-kit-gsd-curated-config).

findings.evidence: The ladder, the config and the catalog are references/subprocess-quota-policy.md, gated for configuring [runner.retry], adding an overlay or interpreting route= and rule=, but sections 6 and 7 still inline the hard-tier cycle, state-file path and stop notices that the reference repeats.
findings.fix: Keep the caller action in sections 6-8 (print the lines, one wait of retry_after_s, abort otherwise, never switch) and point the cycle counts, state-file shape and refusal text at references/subprocess-quota-policy.md under the existing 'read it when you interpret a stop' condition.

findings.evidence: The hard-tier wait is exact (one wait of retry_after_s, never switch), but the Claude Code scheduler branch adds a minute-shifting rule and then says whether the owner runs the printed command is unverified.
findings.fix: Keep the exact wait and the print-and-stop handoff as the default; leave the CronCreate minute rule only under the Claude Code host section of references/launch-and-wait.md, and say the wake is set only after the tool prints a next-run time.

findings.evidence: trigger-queries.json has 8 should-trigger and 8 should-not-trigger queries, short of the about-20 target, and the negatives miss near-misses that share the skill's words (a native Claude Code review, a one-shot session wake, reading a cross-ai log without acting).
findings.fix: Add two should-trigger queries that do not name the runner (a second review round that must keep the session, and an ignored setting the owner must be told about) and two near-miss should-not-trigger queries (review this diff in the current session; schedule a session wake after a usage limit), keeping the 8/8 balance at about 20.

findings.evidence: Six evals cover a casual launch, hosting off, a session resume, id_carries, an auth stop and an argv-file miss, but none asserts the hard-tier branch: exit 75 with retry_after_s= waits once and re-invokes the same lane.
findings.fix: Add one eval whose prompt is an exit-75 lane.err carrying retry_after_s=600, with assertions that the caller waits once for 600 seconds and re-invokes the same runtime, model and role, and does not switch.

findings.evidence: Section 3 says the outer deadline is min(CONFIG outerTimeoutS, GSD's workflow.cross_ai_timeout or gsd-core's 300 s default) and that --outer-timeout replaces that lookup and the CONFIG cap, without saying which number wins when both the flag and the config are set or where the caller reads the value that was used.
findings.fix: State the order in one line: an explicit --outer-timeout is the outer deadline; otherwise the lesser of CONFIG outerTimeoutS and the GSD timeout (300 s when that key is absent); --timeout only lowers the inner deadline; the caller reads the printed deadline, not a second computation.
